thread:
maya: FYI onboarding failed en masse after the RBAC rename last night. SCIM CreateUser returning 500s for several orgs (nova-ops, cypherco, terra-llc). Anyone digging in?

tyler: I saw the alert spikes. Can you drop one of the error lines?

maya: snippet: ```ERROR provisioner: create_user org=cypherco user=jdoe err=500 cause=kms_decrypt_failed details="invalid_ciphertext_or_key" trace=...```

vicky: that smells like KMS key rotation + grant mismatch. Did infra rotate keys?

maya: infra logs show a manual key rotation around 2026-03-19T02:10Z and a terraform apply at 02:16 that touched kms_grant resources.

ron: Access patterns: provisioner stores encrypted ext_id + salt to dedupe. If decrypt fails the code path currently returns a 500 which then causes our duplicate-detection to behave oddly. We should change the error to 409/retryable for these specific KMS errors.

maya: confirmed from KMS audit: ```kms.audit time=2026-03-19T02:11:12Z action=Decrypt key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/old-key used_by=svc:provisioner request_id=x1y2z result=KeyUnavailable``` later entries show `NotFound`.

tyler: KeyUnavailable then NotFound — likely the grant was removed and the new key metadata doesn't include the current service principal. Did the RBAC rename change the assumed-role name used by the provisioner?

vicky: yes, the app-level RBAC rename changed the k8s serviceaccount -> IAM role mapping to provisioner-v2. Previously it was provisioner-v1. Terraform apply recreated grants but used the variable for principal that was still provisioner-v1 due to ordering.

ron: quick mitigation: 1) pause queues for affected orgs so onboarding doesn't churn, 2) create a grant for the provisioner-v2 principal on the active key, 3) run a decrypt probe and replay small batches, 4) patch provisioner to handle decrypt errors more gracefully. Who can take 1/2?

maya: I'll pause the org queues now (nova-ops, cypherco, terra-llc).

infra-bot: deploy 1789 completed 2026-03-19T02:16:05Z by vicky. Changes: aws_kms_key.rotate=true, aws_kms_grant.provisioner -> replaced.

vicky: I'm on step 2, creating an emergency grant for the new principal arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/provisioner-v2. Submitting now.

sec-automation: grant-create requested at 2026-03-19T03:08:22Z by vicky -> grant-id=g-7f8e9d applied to key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/new-key-arn

maya: running decrypt probe for sample ciphertext id=ct-9b8a7 -> `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROV_TOKEN" https://provisioner.internal/ops/decrypt?ct=ct-9b8a7` returned 200 and payload decrypted. Good.

tyler: start a cautious replay of nova-ops only (smallish). Watch for validation failures vs decryption. Keep other orgs paused.

maya: replay started: batch 25 -> 23 success, 2 failed for duplicate email checks (expected). No kms 500s seen.

ron: next steps for postmortem: - enforce IaC ordering so grants get created/updated before role name changes; - include a deploy-time canary that runs a decrypt probe after any key rotation/change; - change provisioner error handling for KMS failures to return retryable status codes and log classification; - plan a rewrap job to migrate stored ciphertexts to new key material (org-by-org).

vicky: agreed. I'll file the terraform change to derive principal dynamically from the live mapping and add a depend_on for grants. Also will prepare a small PR to update kms key policy to reference role tags instead of hard principals.

sec-automation: incident logged INC-2026-1439 category=kms/identity impact=medium owner=maya teams=eng-security,infra,devex

maya: adding notes to the incident doc and will assign owners for postmortem items. If anyone needs raw audit lines or grant ids, DM me. :thumbsup:
